pointers.sentence: `Storage` settles the name in methods its backends inherit; a backend stores the bytes under it, and answers for it (`django/core/files/storage/base.py:Storage`).

Its default has two aliases, `"default"`, a `FileSystemStorage`, and `"staticfiles"`, the static files' storage ([Content types, static files and the other contrib apps](../contrib.md)) (`django/conf/global_settings.py`).

It copies the setting into `StorageHandler.backends` the first time a storage is asked for, and `StorageHandler.__getitem__` makes an alias's storage with `StorageHandler.create_storage` once and keeps it, so the process has one storage for each alias, shared by every thread (`django/core/files/storage/handler.py:StorageHandler`).

`django.core.files.storage.default_storage` is a `DefaultStorage`, a `LazyObject` that looks up the `"default"` alias at first use and stands for it from then on; a `django.db.models.FileField` given no storage keeps it ([File fields](../models/files.md)) (`django/core/files/storage/__init__.py:DefaultStorage`).
A test's override of `STORAGES` empties the handler and the lazy storages ([Overriding settings](../startup/overrides.md)) (`django/test/signals.py:storages_changed`).

Two public methods of `Storage` hand the work to private ones that the base class does not define: `Storage.open` calls `_open`, and `Storage.save`, once it has settled the name, calls `_save` (`django/core/files/storage/base.py:Storage`).
The documentation lets a backend leave some out (`docs/howto/custom-file-storage.txt`), but the inherited `is_name_available` calls `exists`, so `save` needs it.
`Storage.save` takes a name, the content and, optionally, a maximum length, and returns the name it used (`django/core/files/storage/base.py:Storage.save`).

Each check is `validate_file_name`, which raises `SuspiciousFileOperation` for a name whose last part is empty, `"."` or `".."`, or which, read with forward slashes, is absolute or has `".."` among its parts (`django/core/files/utils.py:validate_file_name`).
`Storage.get_available_name` refuses a directory with `".."` among its parts and validates the file name (`django/core/files/storage/base.py:Storage.get_available_name`).

`Storage.get_valid_name` calls `get_valid_filename`, which strips the ends, turns spaces into underscores and drops every character but letters and digits of any script, dashes, underscores and dots; a result that is empty, `"."` or `".."` raises `SuspiciousFileOperation` (`django/utils/text.py:get_valid_filename`).

`Storage.generate_filename` cleans the last part of a path so, refuses `".."` in its directory, and normalizes it (`django/core/files/storage/base.py:Storage.generate_filename`); a file field calls it on the name its `upload_to` gives ([File fields](../models/files.md)).
The constructor of `FileSystemStorage` stores its arguments and reads no setting (`django/core/files/storage/filesystem.py:FileSystemStorage`).

The storage uses cached properties, each the argument or, where that is `None`, a setting read at first use: `FileSystemStorage.location`, `MEDIA_ROOT`, made absolute either way; `FileSystemStorage.base_url`, `MEDIA_URL` (an argument gets a slash at its end); and the two modes, from `FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS` (`0o644`) and `FILE_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY_PERMISSIONS` (`None`) (`django/conf/global_settings.py`).

The constructor connects `StorageSettingsMixin._clear_cached_properties` to `setting_changed`, which drops a property when its setting changes (`django/core/files/storage/mixins.py:StorageSettingsMixin`).

The class is `deconstructible`, as a storage must be for its field to go into a migration (`docs/howto/custom-file-storage.txt`), and the decorator keeps only the arguments given (`django/utils/deconstruct.py:deconstructible`): the example's default storage deconstructs to its class's path and no arguments, naming no directory ([Serializing values: `serializer_factory` and `deconstruct`](../migrations/serializer.md)).

The class is `deconstructible`, as a storage must be for its field to go into a migration (`docs/howto/custom-file-storage.txt`), and the decorator keeps only the arguments given (`django/utils/deconstruct.py:deconstructible`): the example's default storage deconstructs to its class's path and no arguments, naming no directory ([Serializing values: `serializer_factory` and `deconstruct`](../migrations/serializer.md)).

`FileSystemStorage._save` finds the path with `safe_join`, which raises `SuspiciousFileOperation` for one outside the location (`django/utils/_os.py:safe_join`), and makes the missing directories, with `safe_makedirs` when a directory mode is set, since `os.makedirs` does not give the directories between its mode (the comment cites CPython issue 86533).

Other content it writes chunk by chunk, under an exclusive lock (`django/core/files/locks.py`), into a file opened with `os.O_CREAT` and `os.O_EXCL`, so that the open fails if the file exists (`django/core/files/storage/filesystem.py:FileSystemStorage._save`).

Other content it writes chunk by chunk, under an exclusive lock (`django/core/files/locks.py`), into a file opened with `os.O_CREAT` and `os.O_EXCL`, so that the open fails if the file exists (`django/core/files/storage/filesystem.py:FileSystemStorage._save`).

With `allow_overwrite=True`, `FileSystemStorage.is_name_available` considers only the length and `FileSystemStorage.get_alternative_name` returns the name unchanged, so a long name is only cut; `_save` opens with `os.O_TRUNC` in place of `os.O_EXCL`, and lets `file_move_safe` overwrite (`django/core/files/storage/filesystem.py:FileSystemStorage.is_name_available`).
The times are aware, in UTC, under `USE_TZ`, and naive local ones otherwise (`django/core/files/storage/filesystem.py:FileSystemStorage._datetime_from_timestamp`).

`InMemoryStorage` keeps its files in the instance, in a tree of nodes whose files are each an `InMemoryFileNode`, a `ContentFile` that keeps its times (`django/core/files/storage/memory.py:InMemoryStorage`).

It inherits the naming and, given no location or base URL, takes them from `MEDIA_ROOT` and `MEDIA_URL`, but writes nothing to disk; the documentation offers it to speed up tests (`docs/ref/files/storage.txt`).
